methods.notes: The PM advertises the C2 base UUID in its scan response and its GAP name reads "PM5 <serial>". Filter by the name prefix or the base UUID.

device.name: Concept2 Performance Monitor 5 (PM5)
device.notes:
The PM5 is the Performance Monitor on Concept2's RowErg, SkiErg and BikeErg. Concept2 PUBLISHES its BLE interface specification, so this is a friendly documented_api target: pure peer-to-peer BLE (the PM5 is the peripheral), no cloud, no account.
CUSTOM BASE UUID: CE06xxxx-43E5-11E4-916C-0800200C9A66, where the `06` 16-bit slot varies per service/characteristic. The PM advertises the base UUID in its scan response; the GAP device name (0x2A00) reads "PM5 <serial>".
SERVICES (on the C2 base UUID):
  0x0010 Device Information — model 0x0011, serial 0x0012, hardware rev 0x0013,
         firmware rev 0x0014, manufacturer 0x0015 ("Concept2"), erg machine
         type 0x0016, ATT MTU 0x0017, LL DLE 0x0018
  0x0020 Control — receive 0x0021 (WRITE, a CSAFE command frame TO the PM),
         transmit 0x0022 (READ/notify, the CSAFE response FROM the PM)
  0x0030 Rowing — general status 0x0031 (19 B), additional-status-1 0x0032
         (17 B), additional-status-2 0x0033 (20 B), plus stroke/split/force
         characteristics 0x0035-0x003B
Workouts are set up and queried by writing CSAFE command frames to the control receive characteristic; live metrics stream on the Rowing service notifications. On Android an extra multiplexed characteristic packs several status characteristics into one (last byte identifies which).

openness.notes: Concept2 publishes the interface definition; nothing here was reverse- engineered. The CSAFE command set carried inside the control characteristics is a separate published Concept2 document.

credentials.notes: No pairing secret; connection is by proximity/user-confirm on the monitor.

factory_reset.description:
A three-handed gesture: two buttons on the front held while a third, recessed on the back, is pressed and released. Getting it wrong just reboots the monitor, so the confirmation to watch for is the monitor saying it is setting factory defaults — release only then.
Offload anything worth keeping first. The USB Logbook path can export results to a flash drive before the reset removes them.
factory_reset.effect: Wipes every stored workout from the monitor's memory, including the lifetime meters — which for a rower is usually the whole point of the device's history and cannot be recovered afterwards. Settings return to factory defaults.

procedures.basis: Concept2's community forum and the vendor's own PM5 troubleshooting pages, which give the same sequence. Not run against a monitor here.
procedures.indicator: The monitor displays that it is setting factory defaults.
procedures.name: Units and Display held while the rear reset button is pressed

steps.action: Press and hold both the Units and the Display buttons on the front of the PM5.
While still holding them, press and release the recessed reset button on the back, below and to the right of the battery door.
Keep holding the two front buttons until the monitor says it is setting factory defaults, then release.
steps.expect: Factory-defaults message on the display; all stored results and the lifetime meters are gone.

methods.description: On the PM5, turn wireless on. Scan for "PM5 <serial>", connect, subscribe to the Rowing service notifications, and write CSAFE command frames to the control receive characteristic (0x0021) reading responses on 0x0022.

steps.action: On the PM5, More Options -> Turn Wireless ON.
Connect, subscribe to Rowing notifications (0x0031/0x0032/0x0033), read Device Info.

setup.notes: No auth keys or pairing secret: enable wireless on the monitor's menu (More Options -> Turn Wireless ON) and connect. Confidence high — read directly from the vendor spec.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; a new client connects independently.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The custom base UUID, the three services and their characteristics, and the CSAFE-over-control-point design are paraphrased from Concept2's own published PM5 BLE interface definition (rev 1.30).

characteristics.name: Serial number (0x0012)
characteristics.notes: PM serial (also in the GAP name 'PM5 <serial>').

characteristics.name: CSAFE receive (0x0021)
characteristics.notes: Write a CSAFE command frame (up to 20 bytes) TO the PM to set up workouts / query.

characteristics.name: CSAFE transmit (0x0022)
characteristics.notes: The CSAFE response frame FROM the PM.

characteristics.name: General status (0x0031)
characteristics.notes: 19 bytes: elapsed time (3 B, 0.01 s), distance (3 B, 0.1 m), workout type, interval type, workout state, rowing state, stroke state, total work distance (3 B), workout duration (3 B), duration type, drag factor.

characteristics.name: Additional status 1 (0x0032)
characteristics.notes: 17 bytes: elapsed time, speed (0.001 m/s), stroke rate, heart rate (bpm, 255 invalid), current pace, average pace, rest distance, rest time, erg machine type.

characteristics.name: Additional status 2 (0x0033)
characteristics.notes: 20 bytes: elapsed time, interval count, average power (W), total calories, split/interval average pace/power/calories, last split time/distance.
